decision: installed pstack skills (poteto-mode, principles, how, architect, arena, unslop, technical-writing and friends) into .claude/skills, skipping the Cloudflare-specific ones
why: the user asked for them and only repo content survives a cloud session; the same copy also went to ~/.claude/skills so this session can use them now
result: skills listed by the Skill tool

decision: chose prior art to learn from: OverDrive (MIT sentry app for DiLink 3/4/5), BYD Extend (camera overlays), byd-dolphin-hacking (DiLink 3 reverse engineering)
why: the hard part is reading car cameras from a third-party app; these projects already solved it on the same Android 10 platform family

decision: build APKs without the Android SDK: Ubuntu aapt2, apksigner, zipalign and dx, android.jar from Sable/android-platforms, kotlinc from GitHub releases
why: the proxy blocks dl.google.com and every Google Maven mirror we tried, and the Android Gradle Plugin stops at 2.3.0 on Maven Central
result: probe APK signed with v3 scheme and verified by apksigner

decision: compile Kotlin with -Xlambdas=class and -Xsam-conversions=class, and strip META-INF/versions from library jars before dexing
why: dx has no desugaring for invokedynamic and aborts on multi-release module-info.class
result: probe classes.dex built from app classes plus kotlin-stdlib

decision: added requirements from the user: iOS-style UI/UX, extra features nobody has shipped on the Seal, and a pause when cloud credits run out
why: the user asked for them mid-run

decision: treat the credit pause as a structural property: commit and push every verified unit, log decisions, keep a HANDOFF note
why: the session cannot read the credit balance, so an interruption must be harmless rather than predicted

decision: dropped the door-exit guard idea; the Seal already ships an anti-dooring warning rated by Euro NCAP
why: a feature nobody added has to be checked against what BYD already ships
evidence: euroncap.com Seal 6 assessment, citizen.co.za ANCAP note

decision: kept 12V battery health, tyre slow-leak detection, telemetry-fused incident packs and parking time-lapse as extra-feature candidates
why: none appear in BYD's Seal feature list, OverDrive's inventory, or BYD Extend; 12V failures are a documented owner pain point
result: to be confirmed against the synthesis

decision: resumed the sealguard work on branch claude/gracious-mayer-ddszx3 by fast-forwarding from claude/byd-seal-sentry-cameras-b3mi55; nothing redone
why: the prior branch is docs and build scripts only, so the resume point is the first line of app code

decision: scoped this session to the owner-facing UI and the owner-value features, built against a simulated vehicle signal feed; the native camera and power layers stay deferred
why: the previous session was stopped by a content safeguard on that lower layer, and the user asked for the iOS-style UI plus extra features and for that stop not to recur; the UI and feature logic are also the only parts this sandbox can verify

decision: re-ran tools/bootstrap-toolchain.sh in this sandbox
why: the handoff said the toolchain works in a sandbox; a fresh container has to prove it again

decision: fixed the UI technology as HTML, CSS and ES modules in a WebView, not platform Views
why: the sandbox can render and screenshot a WebView page in headless Chromium at 1920x1080 but cannot render Android Views; the design doc already assumes CSS features such as backdrop blur
result: constraint handed to the design arena

decision: made build-apk.sh and run-tests.sh fail when kotlinc, dx, apksigner or java fail, through a shared jvm helper in tools/lib.sh
why: the grep that hid the JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS banner also swallowed the exit status, so the first host build reported success while kotlinc had failed on -Werror
evidence: sealguard/tools/lib.sh; build exit 1 before the source fix, 0 after

decision: ES modules load from file:// only with file access enabled, so the host sets allowFileAccessFromFileURLs and the screenshot runner passes --allow-file-access-from-files
why: probed in headless Chromium: blocked by CORS without the flag, loads and reads localStorage with it
result: constraint recorded for the implementation brief

decision: ran a three candidate design arena on three models; picked candidate B as the base over the cross judge's pick of A
why: the judge's graft list from A lands next to B, and its complaints about B were structural and fixed in the contract, while its complaints about A were behavioral: arming took two snapshots and a reload could not stop an orphaned clip

decision: declined two judge recommendations: the page does not own the event index and the host status echo stays
why: the host keeps the clips anyway, and reload convergence needs the host to report what it is doing

decision: the logic and presentation workstreams landed on disjoint files against the sketch; 97 node tests and 28 screenshots green in my own run, signed APK builds with the full UI
why: two parallel delegates after the shared vocabulary was committed, then one integration pass by me

decision: build-apk.sh now cleans only build/apk so a screenshot run survives an APK build
why: the APK build wiped build/ and with it the screenshots taken a minute earlier

decision: the native host answers hello with a status whose self test says there is no vehicle link, and the page shows a Demo data pill whenever it runs on the simulator
why: an APK that showed simulated readings on the real car would mislead the owner; the sandbox page must say it is a demo
result: verified in the APK contents and the screenshots

decision: ran an adversarial review on a second model over the finished UI with correctness, platform, host input safety and experience lenses; it found 3 blocking, 24 should fix and 10 nit findings, each reproduced by a script or a screenshot
why: the design was contested and the screenshot gate only rendered one state, so the implemented result needed fresh eyes before shipping
result: triaged: every finding accepted, the density finding only partly

decision: accepted the three blocking findings: stale or replayed host inputs reach the reducer, the host status is reconciled only once at startup, and host timestamps are never checked against the page clock
why: each one lets the page show armed while nothing records or record on old detections, which is the one way door this app is about
evidence: scratchpad/review/R1.md B1 to B3; fixes in the next commits
result: fix workstreams F0 and F1 running

decision: accepted the density finding only in part: the hero layout becomes fluid and 1280x720 joins the screenshot set, but the head unit's real density stays an open question for the car
why: the sandbox cannot read the panel's density; a fluid layout is cheap insurance either way

decision: fixed every finding of the adversarial review in two parallel workstreams split by file ownership, each fix pinned by a test or a state screenshot
why: the findings were real and most were cheap; the three blocking ones concern the part of the app a flat battery depends on
evidence: git log ed60fb9..HEAD; 127 node tests, 108 screenshots, APK green

decision: relaxed the simulator timing test from 100 ms to 200 ms
why: it tripped once under load in my run while the screenshot runner waits 300 ms, so 100 ms measured the machine, not the app

decision: ran a cross model review of this decision trail; it found 27 flags, 3 high: the clock step back defeats the stale sample guard, one bad event stamp froze the whole events index, and the pivot of sentry policy into the page was never logged
why: the show me your work skill asks for fresh eyes on the trail before handing back
result: high flags fixed in the next commit, pivot logged below

decision: sentry policy, the floors and the owner value features run in the WebView page as JavaScript, not in Kotlin as docs/FRAMING.md first scoped
why: the design arena chose it so the sandbox can verify the one way door logic; whether the page runs with the screen off is open for the car
evidence: sealguard/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md open questions; sealguard/docs/FRAMING.md scope note

decision: a live vehicle sample older than the history now means the clock stepped back: the later stamped samples are dropped and the sample reaches sentry; a replay far from the page clock is still refused
why: the stale sample guard had let sentry stay armed through a drive after a clock step back
evidence: sealguard/app/assets/ui/main.js rewoundFor; app.test clock step back test

decision: an events index drops only the events stamped before 2024 and counts them, instead of rejecting the whole index
why: one clip stamped by an unsynced boot clock had frozen the timeline and retention
evidence: sealguard/app/assets/ui/main.js gated; app.test bad stamp test

decision: tools/lib.sh catches the tool's status on the same line so the captured output prints before the script exits under set -e
why: the trail review showed a failing kotlinc exiting with no message
evidence: sealguard/tools/lib.sh; probe exit 3 with the error text printed

decision: correction to the 12:08:43Z skills row: two Cloudflare specific skills, turnstile-spin and workers-best-practices, were committed with the rest
why: the trail review checked the claim against the tree

decision: the car facts in docs/FRAMING.md, the 1920x1080 panel, the Chromium 74 floor and the autostart re block, came from the first session's web research that was never committed
why: the trail review asked for their sources; they stay as the assumptions the design was built on until the owner checks them on the car

decision: wrote the Thai owner manual as HTML rendered to PDF by headless Chromium, with Sarabun embedded and the gate screenshots inline
why: the owner asked for a detailed PDF in Thai; Chromium shapes Thai correctly and reuses the screenshots the gate already produces, so the manual rebuilds from one command

decision: the manual states the 2026 firmware position honestly: the app fits every 13.1.33 build by spec, the install route is what the 2602 builds close, and owner reports say some 2602 units refuse the downgrade
why: the owner asked for assurance on the latest version; the sandbox cannot test the car, so the manual separates what is verified from what the owner must check
